  • Hack ’95 is being developed by a team of industry veterans with experience at SEGA, Rovio, Disney, TikTok, and Adult Swim, with a script overseen by international bestselling author (A Boy Made of Blocks) and veteran games journalist (The Guardian) Keith Stuart.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PQube will publish Village Studio-developed card-based hacking adventure game Hack ’95 when it rolls out for PC via Steam in 2027, the companies revealed.

Hack ’95 is being developed by a team of industry veterans with experience at SEGA, Rovio, Disney, TikTok, and Adult Swim, with a script overseen by international bestselling author (A Boy Made of Blocks) and veteran games journalist (The Guardian) Keith Stuart.

Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page:.

Welcome to the dawn of the Internet. Your best friend, elite hacker mega_hurtz, is missing, presumed dead. All signs point to an assassination by the Federal Bureau of Cyber Security and the all-powerful Axis Megasystems. To uncover the truth, you’ll need illegal scripts and righteous hardware to hack your way through the Bureau’s high-security House of Cards network.

In a recent development, hack ’95 is a card-based hacking adventure set inside Navigate ’95, a ‘state-of-the-art’ operating system featuring multitasking and CD-quality sound. Chat with the freaks and geeks of cyberspace’s underbelly, who task you with defeating security systems and snooping through compromised desktops. All to unravel a conspiracy more sinister than you could ever imagine.

In a recent development, no coding skills? No problem! All you need is a deck, a 56kbps modem, and a healthy disregard for authority.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although GTA 6 continues to smash records as the highest-rated game of all time, it hasn't been without any bugs to speak of – some of which are proving so persistent, Rockstar's own patches aren't wiping them out of the new Grand Theft Auto game.

It has been revealed that one especially notorious bug – a bug that Rockstar's first GTA 6 upgrade didn't manage to tackle despite promising to – sees players' in-game weather locked. If you didn't already know it, the weather is supposed to be dynamic (realistic, even), changing over time from sunny to rainy to stormy to… you get it. Unfortunately, though, it's not properly swapping for many fans, resulting in a far more stagnant experience and reduced immersion. And while the recent GTA 6 patch apparently didn't fix the bug for affected players, fans on Twitter have come to the rescue. "I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6," one writes. "You just have to clear your PS5's cache. It's super easy and takes like two minutes." They then outline how to do so, from shutting down their PlayStation 5 to clearing the system cache in safe mode.

Industry observers note that I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6. LETS GOOOO. You just have to clear your PS5’s cache. It’s super easy and takes like two minutes. > Turn off your PS5 completely. > Press and hold the power button until it beeps to enter safe mode. > Go to option 6 and select clear system cache. > Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed. I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted, thank you so much to @mauricioce85796 for leaving a reply advising me to do this. Unreal that this wasn’t patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.November 26, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that "Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed," they state, going on to say it took them quite some time to figure the fix out. "I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven't experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm." The poster credits a fellow fan for the fix, concluding that it's "unreal that this wasn't patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.".

In a recent development, comments see other players thanking the two for the fix and confirming that it does indeed work. "Can confirm," reads on. "Weather is more varied!" Another adds, "It worked for me too! I'd never seen storm clouds forming like that in my 50 hours of gameplay!" Hopefully, however, Rockstar rolls out another official fix soon, and fans don't feel the need to crack into their PS5's deeper settings to get weather working.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos.
  • Industry observers note that marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018.
  • In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the firm and if what they were doing was legitimate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos. Now, everyone from former employees to psychologists is weighing in on Holmes both before and after her fraud convictions led to a long prison sentence that she is at the moment serving in Texas. Recently, one of Holmes’ assistants, Aria Marinelli, from the early days of Theranos, appeared on the Assistants vs. Agents podcast and spoke about a few red flags she saw in her short time working for the disgraced CEO.

Industry observers note that marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018. Holmes went to prison in 2023. Marinelli wasn’t at the company long, by the sound of things, but did work directly for Holmes in her time with the Silicon Valley startup that promised big things with what we now know was a completely fraudulent blood-testing machine (a machine Marinelli notes she never even laid eyes on until seeing You Can See Everything).

In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the firm and if what they were doing was legitimate. According to Marinelli, the suspicions started even before she accepted the job, as she explained:.

It has been revealed that I went and looked through old emails just to see if I was remembering correctly, and it turns out I was. So this is [an email to] a mentor of mine. I said: ‘It's looking like I have to get Theranos an answer tomorrow regarding their offer. It expires at COB, and they've already extended it once. I'm very hesitant to accept because the work and the work environment are really not my ideal next step. Something about it doesn't sit right, I guess.’.

Sources indicate that she went on to explain that pretty early on, there was never a lot of talk about what the organization was trying to do with the machine. In typical Silicon Valley style, according to Marinelli, most of the talk was about stock shares, IPOs, and how much money they could all make. That was something else that didn’t sit right with her.

Sources indicate that not only did Marinelli never see the now-infamous device, but she never saw a blood testing lab at all and was worried that despite famous names on the board of directors, there seemed to be no one with medical knowledge. That also raised concerns for her, as she explained:.

The biggest thing was that there was no lab. So I had noticed that there were no doctors on the board, and that's, again, been talked about ad nauseam, but I was willing to dismiss that as maybe they were just getting started, right? And I remember just being told, ‘Oh, it's off-site,’ but I never saw anybody in that time frame that was working in a lab or that was from that lab.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the organization’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:.

In a recent development, everyone [at Theranos] is very secretive, very, you know, shielded in how they're speaking about this thing. I doubt they would just ship it off to someone and not have them have a concerted program around testing it. So that, to me, was kind of the last flag that I was willing to put up with.

According to recent reports, marinelli also gave her honest impression of Holmes, and it wasn’t all negative, but she did mention that she thought The Dropout, the series starring Amanda Seyfried that can be seen with a Hulu subscription, is a fair portrayal of Holmes as Marinelli knew her. She also praised You Can See Everything and seems to have real sympathy for Holmes, saying, “everyone has to lie at that level.”.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that one of the many interesting and brilliant things about You Can See Everything is that everyone sees something different in it, including the people who worked for Holmes and Theranos, and I don’t think this is the last time we’ll hear from people who worked with her and knew her. Especially as this movie continues to get Oscar buzz and will continue to be in the cultural zeitgeist for some time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping.
  • In a recent development, the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux.
  • Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, fresh Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

In a recent development, the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she mentioned with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

According to recent reports, when pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux stated. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

In a recent development, bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

Originally published by Vanity Fair France.

Ubisoft now require their devs to explain why they aren't using genAI in game pitches, claims report, though the Assassin's Creed publishers deny they're mandating it

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (435 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing latest games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule.
  • The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having stated that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.
  • Ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the company are all in on generative AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing latest games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule. The publishers' statement comes in the wake of a report claiming that Ubisoft devs with pitches that don't use genAI are required to explain in detail why they've decided it isn't suitable for the game being outlined.

The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having stated that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.

Ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the company are all in on generative AI. They cited an "attitude shift" among Ubisoft management as having left workers feeling "cornered by generative AI all the time", but made clear Ubisoft haven't brought in a blanket mandate forcing devs to use genAI no matter what.

It has been revealed that ubisoft have emphasised the latter in a statement subsequently issued to Vertical Slice. "We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work," the company wrote. "This doesn’t mean that projects are required to use generative AI. Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to create for players.".

Ubisoft have been keen on experimenting with genAI in game development for a little while - something essentially set in stone by the establishing of Motherbrain as a proper division where the company can work on the likes of the "first playable generative AI experience" they were shouting about earlier this year. That move came in a year Ubisoft have spent vast swaths of laying off staff and closing studios, as part of a restructuring they kicked off with a barrage of cancellations in January.

Most recently, those cuts hit 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on a list of other affected subsidiaries that I'm very much getting tired of wheeling out whenever Ubisoft inevitably insist on adding to it.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

GTA 6 launch knocked Call of Duty's daily players down 42 percent, Alinea estimates

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (535 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.
  • Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.
  • According to recent reports, "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

According to recent reports, "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

Fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active users across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr.

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

Elliott noted the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the big live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

According to recent reports, elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he states, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 released on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6.

Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist, says he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.

In a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he says he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”. He’s credited as a developer on the Physics Development Group, and he said in his video that the entire team was “amazing”.

The Edinburgh-based dev is no stranger to real-life racing, as it fielded its own winning team in the 24 Hours of Nürburgring event four years ago. Ben Lyons, who made up part of the squad, was the Technical Director in charge of physics on the title.

I personally really love the way cars feel in the game.

Each type has its own distinctive handling model, and you can really feel the difference when you go to a Mod Shop and tune your car to taste.

It doesn’t have the distinctive heavy handling of GTA 4, but it’s also not quite as arcadey as GTA 5 either – I’d say it sits somewhere comfortably between the two, which is a good place to be.

I love all the extra work that’s been put into the DualSense’s haptic feedback, too; the way you can physically feel the change of grip between the different road surfaces – it’s impressive stuff.

Sources indicate that I just wish Rockstar had put a little more energy into the races themselves, because they do rely on aggressive rubber banding, which is pretty frustrating. Considering how meticulously the rest of the game is crafted, it would have been nice if a bit more thought went into this aspect.

In a recent development, all in all, though, I’m not surprised to learn GTA 6 had real-life race car drivers and pro Gran Turismo players on its team. You spend a good chunk of your time in Leonida driving, and I think by and large Rockstar really nailed this notable aspect of the game.

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-new game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

It has been revealed that thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

According to recent reports, but I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the significant names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

In a recent development, in fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most crucial bits.

A new and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

Price check: Amazon $29.99 (Grey).

Industry observers note that out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

It's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

We've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery.

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple).

Industry observers note that but if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, at the moment going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

Recent findings suggest that finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

Recent findings suggest that it's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

A modder using AI to create The Last of Us Part 2 multiplayer that Naughty Dog never gave us states Sony can't do much even if it wanted to shut it down.

Earlier this year, Sony put the brakes on one such mod. YouTuber Speclizer announced their mod at the start of this year, but two months ago, they announced it was canceled after they received a cease and desist from Sony Interactive Entertainment. However, another has emerged in the form of Twelve Weeks (via IGN), with the developer releasing a mod earlier this week featuring 4v4 team battles.

The creator, Kellie, admitted on Twitter that AI was used in its development, saying, "Claude code was used for most of the project." However, they note that no AI artwork has been used, with the dev explaining she made the artwork herself.

Over on a YouTube video for the mod, the developer's account claims that Speclizer's mod was subject to a cease and desist because it was paywalled, but "mine is released already for free and in open source." However, even if the devs do receive a letter from Sony, it's claimed that "since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down.".

In a recent development, naughty Dog was creating The Last of Us Online based on the second game for some time before it was canceled in 2023. Word out of the studio was very favorable, with its director, Vinit Agarwal, saying some who worked on it thought it was "the best multiplayer game they've ever played.".

It has been revealed that the Last of Us had a shockingly great multiplayer mode, strong enough to rival other substantial hitters of the Xbox 360 and PS3 generation. Who knows how the sequel's would've been, but with how much better the gameplay was in The Last of Us Part 2 was, I reckon it could've been great.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that yesterday I made a significant error in judgement. In writing an apology to our readers, I made a target of one of our writers and I won't be able to undo that. What I can try to do is apologise to that writer, who I'm addressing now.

It has been revealed that my failures towards you were several. Firstly, in not explaining that we are able to step in by replying to and moderating comments when a discussion is becoming heated or aggressive, I never made it clear there were protections available to you that you weren't receiving.

Secondly, for mentioning you at all in the apology. While I hoped to make it clear to readers we wouldn't disrespect them in future, I laid the blame for that on your feet in public. The responsibility of an editor is to protect their writers, and I failed you profoundly.

Thirdly, that I didn't speak to you ahead of the post. As far as you were concerned the matter was settled, and I then put it in public without any warning.

According to recent reports, fourth, while we often talk of RPS being a collection of different writers with different viewpoints, where no one member of the team has the definitive view on a subject, this creates a vacuum for our contributors to operate in. This means fresh writers have very little direction when it comes to how they approach any topic and the response their work may receive. Again, any failings here are ultimately my responsibility.

Sources indicate that finally, this failure is all the more significant because it has happened across lines of gender privilege. RPS has a full-time staff of cisgender men, which inevitably gives rise to bias and ignorance we must actively confront, while we work towards being in a position to address our lack of gender diversity, beyond commissioning the occasional marginalised freelance writer. Non-cisgender writers are both much more exposed to abuse and much less favoured in terms of steady work. As such, a public rebuke from your own editor is far more damaging than it would be if the freelancer were a cisgender man. On this count, I have been extremely thoughtless in ways that would likely not have been the case when this site had a majority female editorship.

Ashley, I am deeply sorry that I let you down in these ways.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that "First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has mentioned people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

Industry observers note that "First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development plans for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

Recent findings suggest that "Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" stated Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.".

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski said nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

In a recent development, "I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he noted.

Sources indicate that "They're ambition-driven developments and money's important - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I said, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that.".

According to recent reports, when asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he noted.

Statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not launched on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

"And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4.".

Finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

Sources indicate that "The most notable takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski mentioned. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

Industry observers note that "If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future.".

It has been revealed that CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The company made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game upgrade, went a long way.

Recent findings suggest that the Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription. While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats, I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a significant impact on the semifinals episode.

Following Connie's truly heartbreaking elimination, the semifinal episode of Bake Off featured the top four contestants creating Patisseries. There was just one big problem: the heat wave in the U.K. was making it especially hot in the iconic tent. Unfortunately that threw a wrench into the baker's prepares, especially when they needed the time to cool their bakes. I thought this was going to be a big problem over the course of the season, and I feel totally vindicated after watching the semifinal episode of the season.

Industry observers note that the struggle of cooling bakes has been a recurring theme throughout this season of Bake Off, and it had major implications during Patisserie week. This was especially true for the technical challenge, where contestants needed to create judge Paul Hollywood's Gateau Concorde in 21⁄2 hours. Inside the tent was reportedly a whopping 94 degrees, and a number of the bakes suffered as a result.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had concerns with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show, so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

The Great British Baking Show releases upcoming episodes of Netflix as part of the 2026 TV schedule. I've had a blast enjoying my first full season of the long-running competition series, and I'll definitely be back to watch the next season.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.
  • With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and stated, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Latest York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

It has been revealed that right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Upcoming York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

Recent findings suggest that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a massive fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

Recent findings suggest that she's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

In a recent development, what she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

In a recent development, mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

He said, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she remarked, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

It makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

In a recent development, the way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had noted that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so massive, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I stated, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

According to recent reports, yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

Industry observers note that what was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Sources indicate that mckenna knew back in April, she stated, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me fresh references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

Recent findings suggest that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

Industry observers note that that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom noted, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

It has been revealed that I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a big franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has mentioned, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a significant fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

Industry observers note that I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

Recent findings suggest that the looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How key is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

Recent findings suggest that what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It has been revealed that it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

Recent findings suggest that in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the New York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

In the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Sources indicate that pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

So when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and said, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

According to recent reports, what's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend said, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

"This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced.
  • According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".
  • Industry observers note that speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".

Industry observers note that speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for fresh kinds of conversation to start happening," reads the union statement. "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We head from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.

"A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," they continue. "But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.".

In a recent development, the Rockstar UK unionisation drive has been a long journey. The vote follows open confrontation between Rockstar management in the UK and IWGB-affiliated Rockstar employees working out of a private Discord server. After allegedly keeping the Discord server under surveillance for over two years, Rockstar bosses fired around 30 staff in October 2026 on charges of "gross misconduct" and breach of confidentiality. The IWGB and the fired workers have countered by accusing Rockstar of union-busting, observing that the Discord's putative union membership had reached the 10% minimum required for statutory recognition under UK law, shortly before the firings.

Recent findings suggest that 220 Rockstar staff subsequently signed an open letter to management calling for the reinstatement of the fired workers. The IWGB also organised protest rallies outside the offices of Rockstar North in Edinburgh and Take-Two Interactive in London. A UK Member of Parliament weighed in, calling on ministers to "stop this from happening again". Finally, the ousted workers took Rockstar to court in an employment tribunal that has run for much of this year: the closing statements landed on the eve of GTA 6's release, with a judge's verdict pending.

I'm sorry to see the union vote fall through, given the boost a formally recognised GTA developer union in the UK would have given to labour organisation across the industry. In the short term, of course, it might have made for a safer and more supportive workplace at Rockstar. While there is relatively little recent reporting on current working conditions, many Rockstar games are allegedly the product of "crunch culture", stemming back to the development of the first 3D Grand Theft Autos on PS2.

In January 2010, an anonymous user posting on behalf of the “wives of Rockstar San Diego employees" claimed that staff had been forced to work 12-hour, six day weeks to finish the first Red Dead Redemption. A landmark report from Kotaku in 2018, based on interviews with 34 current and 43 former employees, described developers piling up evening and weekend work across Rockstar's empire, with crunch especially severe among QA staff at Rockstar Lincoln in the UK.

Industry observers note that some of Kotaku's sources mentioned they had been explicitly pushed to work overtime by managers, facilitated by workplace systems such as hour-logging. Others spoke of a more vaporous expectation that they put in inhuman effort, because after all, working at the studio behind GTA is a privilege. Many had fond memories of their experiences, even as they acknowledged the toll taken on their minds, bodies and relationships outside work. This is part of the problem with crunch - it doesn't have to be explicitly imposed. It comes about because some creative and enthusiastic people are not good at recognising their own limits, and less scrupulous employers are happy to profit from this and, worse, erect a working culture around it.

Recent findings suggest that the 2018 Kotaku piece acknowledges that some crunch results from the uneven and unpredictable way many videogames are made, but it also talks about overtime brought on by unaccountable leadership, with studio co-founders Dan and Sam Houser "renowned for rebooting, overhauling, and discarding large chunks of their games." (Dan Houser left the firm in 2020.) The same heads were also said to value the "appearance" of developers going the extra mile, with one dev telling the site they were encouraged to walk a lap of the office on Saturday, whenever the Housers were in town. Together with anxieties about confidentiality, that emphasis on devs being visibly busy perhaps informs Rockstar's cancelling of hybrid working in early 2024, which precipitated some of this year's union activism.

It has been revealed that many of the people pushing for unionisation at Rockstar are also reacting to events across the games industry. There has been a huge wave of mass layoffs as companies "adjust" following the boom period initiated by Covid lockdowns. Some of those laid off had recently shipped commercially successful games, like Battlefield 6. GTA 6 developers have publicly expressed concerns about getting cut, even as their upcoming open worlder makes sales records.

A chunk of the recent mass layoffs are owing to lucrative company acquisitions and consolidations that have attracted criticism from existing unions. Microsoft have spent two years axing studios, projects and jobs after spending around $69 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard. EA are now owned by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund and Donald Trump's son-in-law; the company has since laid off hundreds of developers and closed the mighty BioWare as they shoulder an enormous debt, which they're reportedly hoping to offset by means of mass generative AI-powered costcutting. As alluded to in today's IWGB statement, there is the overarching question of how genAI - often explicitly mandated by executives - will threaten livelihoods by automating tasks, giving bosses an excuse to keep headcounts small by one means or another.

The repeated layoff waves have inspired a lot of union action at many large videogame companies, from Microsoft to Ubisoft, but I suspect a lot of that hasn't been apparent outside labour organising and enthusiast circles. GTA is as breakthrough a vidya as you can get. Rockstar forming a union would have been a foundation from which to talk more about worker power beyond the games industry.

As often when reporting on unionisation, I'm left idly wondering about what kind of art a fully unionised industry would create. The production conditions of many games can be deduced from their design – a photorealistic open world game, for example, is a vast assemblage of resources that may hinge on distributed development across an unequal world. Rockstar both represent AAA gaming at its grAAAndest, and have historically been part of the auteur craze, with the Housers having the final say on every detail.

It has been revealed that we are, in general, all very familiar with the caricatures of auteur-led development, positioned as a source of both eccentric brilliance and ruinous hubris. I think there's much less of a narrative for the kind of art you get from teams where workers have serious negotiating power, though there are precedents in the form of cooperatives and similar organisations that tether their labour conditions more boldly to the kind of art they produce: for example, Die Gute Fabrik, and most recently, Summer Eternal.

A unionised Rockstar wouldn't just be a space in which workers are better protected against the expectations of managers and financial stakeholders; you'd get different kinds of art. Maybe more interesting kinds of art! I do wonder if union organisers could do a more effective job of expressing this hope, perhaps exploring where certain games have lost their way because workers were treated like cannon fodder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

According to recent reports, you've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.

The fresh Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.

Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

Recent findings suggest that the exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with upcoming content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

Five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be declared straight afterwards.

Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.

Earlier this month, Valve released a latest Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar knows GTA 6's criminal profile system isn't for everyone, but is keen to stress you're still free to play the newly introduced Grand Theft Auto game however you like.

According to recent reports, as our handy GTA 6 criminal profiles guide explains, the upcoming system riffs on Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor mechanic by tracking your actions to build an overall picture of your behavior and playstyle. It's a system that holds a mirror up to you, but not one that punishes you for how you play. Rather, depending on how you navigate Leonida, the world may react differently to your presence.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, feelings among players are mixed. Plenty enjoy what it adds to the role-playing aspect of GTA 6, whereas others don't like the suggestion that their Vice City rampage is being judged.

Recent findings suggest that none of this is a surprise to Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson. Speaking to VGC ahead of the game's launch, he claims the honor system is designed to enhance the experience rather than detract from it. Regardless, developers knew some players would "reject this upcoming stuff we're offering.".

In a recent development, "I think it opens a latest range of choices and decisions for the player to make," he says. "You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options.".

Nelson goes on to say he hopes the system "changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game.

"In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you're setting these guys up as what they are," he notes.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

In a recent development, "We were conscious of that. Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it's not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They're trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life.".

It has been revealed that nelson then states that Jason is the same. He's still "getting in trouble with Donnie and all that," but has still been enjoying a "relatively criminal-adjacent existence.".

I suppose the element of choice kicks off from there. Do the pair lean into a life of crime for all the fortune it brings, or are they victims of circumstance? The answer depends on what's right for how you want to play the game.

At least, that's how I've been viewing it. The response to GTA 6's criminal profiles has been interesting, and so has the reaction to other optional content. A Valve veteran with credits on Half-Life 2 and more likened players struggling with it to being stuck in "moral yellow paint." Basically, the idea is that other games give you a set lane to operate within, so plenty of people feel like they have to do everything GTA 6 suggests, when you are actually free to ignore it and exist out of that lane.

Regardless, GTA 6 has clearly won out overall. Our GTA 6 review lands on a perfect score, and the fact that the GTA 6 Metacritic score is only rivaled by the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time tells you everything you need to know about what other critics thought. Players have also been more than happy to show what they think through their wallet, with GTA 6 becoming the fastest-selling piece of media ever, beating the likes of Spider-Man: Brand Newly introduced Day and The Odyssey.

Getting started? Check out our GTA 6 guides for everything you need.

When I'm not running the news team on the games side, you'll find me putting News Editor duties to one side to play the hottest JRPG of 20 years ago or pillaging the depths of Final Fantasy 14 for a swanky fresh cloak – the more colourful, the better.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grabbing a Truffade Thrax in GTA 6 isn't too hard, but if you want Andrew Node's supercharged version, the true fastest car around, you'll need to complete a little collectible hunt. Before you start, it's worth noting that this special Truffade Thrax costs 70k to register when you steal it, though you can also sell it to Randy for 20k (not that I would recommend this as it's a unique car).

Industry observers note that the first step is scanning ten No Flusher toilet graffiti stamps around Vice Beach, the east portion of Vice City, with your WAiNK It app. Each symbol is basically a little blue toilet. After that, you'll have to head to a secret lockup, and then you're on for stealing the car.

This first one is southeast of Nola - Ocean beach on the pavement on the west side of the road.

The second is east of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, on the south side pavement of the road leading out onto the grass towards the beach.

This one is at the east end of the bridge leading from Vice Beach to Waxman Island, on the southern pavement. Also to the west of LTD Gas - Ocean Beach.

This fourth one is east of Aural Expert and north of Venus Fitness, on the pavement at the side of the junction.

This one is on the pavement directly in front of Banana Hole Main Bar, east down the road from the previous one above.

This sixth one is on the sidewalk on the far west of the road running along the bottom of the huge park in Vice Beach.

This seventh is west of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, down the road you can see with the roundabout at the end on the map.

The eighth is east down the road from Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank and south of Easy Electronics, on the pavement on the corner.

This ninth is north of Marshal's jewelry and northeast of Endzone - Washington Beach, at the east end of the major carpark bordering the beach.

On the right side of the northern road at the Oldby Island junction, directly opposite Ron Gas - Washington Beach.

After you've found all ten, Cal's conspiracy theory chat (which unlocks after the first) will go dark, before you get a separate message a little later giving you their hideout location. Head there, read the note to the right of the garage door, and then look on the back of it to get the code for the lock:.

Inside you'll have a bunch of evidence pointing to Andrew Node's house on Starfish island, so examine it all and then you're ready to steal the car.

First off, Starfish Island is a gated community with security, so it's better to get a boat there. Head west from the hideout and steal a boat on the piers, then drive west across the water to the jetty of Andrew Node's house—it's the one on the southern side towards the centre, that looks like a backwards L.

It has been revealed that dock, head around the left side of the house to find a white garage on the right you can open up with Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax inside. You'll have to drive it off the island, but after that you can head to Randy and register it for 70k. Just make sure you have the garage space and the money before you steal the car.

Recent findings suggest that the Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

Recent findings suggest that "Fixed an concern where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

In a recent development, there've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an glitch where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

Sources indicate that beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a new build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:.

It has been revealed that generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

It's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that that means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

The news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December.".

Recent findings suggest that that means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

Last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

It has been revealed that lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe.

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Sources indicate that following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the initiative was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

The sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".
