Country music is so much more than an industry — it’s a community filled with supporters and cheerleaders.

Recent findings suggest that need proof? Just look what happened when Us decided to celebrate Thanksgiving by asking artists to share a fellow musician they are grateful for this holiday season.

Time and time again, country singers shared stories of their peers who have offered encouragement, inspiration and friendship in times when it mattered most.

Sources indicate that 9-1-1: Nashville star LeAnn Rimes will never forget the opportunity she got to learn from Reba McEntire during a Dr. Pepper commercial.

As for Lady A’s Dave Haywood, he continues to look up to Tim McGraw for hitting all the right notes when it comes to “work-life balance.”.

Keep reading to see who your favorite country singers are grateful for this Turkey Day:.

I’m thankful for Dolly [Parton]. I am thankful for the light she shined on this world, for all the goodness, for her heart. There will never be anyone like Dolly, and I think she showed us what real heart looks like, and she radiated goodness. I just think we could all learn a thing or two from Dolly. I’m just grateful that we got to have her in all of our lives in this lifetime, and I’m grateful that I got to have the time with her that I did, and she was impactful and inspiring to me as not just an artist, but just as a woman in this world. And I always, like everyone else, I always think, “What would Dolly do?” And she would always meet everything and everyone with kindness.

I’m thankful for my buddy, Thomas Rhett. I’ve known Thomas for a long time now, and I have always been a fan of the way he has approached music and his career while keeping his family first; I’ve always respected that. He’s been a role model to me not just in music, but in life. I love him to death and I’m proud to call him a friend.

It has been revealed that I would absolutely say Willie Nelson. He has had such a huge influence on me, being from Austin, that I just released a Willie Nelson tribute album. He is a true one of one, a legend, an amazing songwriter, and being on stage with him a few times has been a highlight of my career so far.

I’d have to say Carrie Underwood! I remember early on, when I first got to Nashville, we swapped numbers, and I ended up calling her from the side of the road one day just to ask for advice. She was so gracious with her time and encouragement. She’s continued to be such a kind, steady source of encouragement over the years, even from afar. This industry can be a lot to navigate, especially when you’re young and figuring things out, so I’ve always been really grateful for the kindness she’s shown me. I grew up listening to her music and have looked up to her for a long time, so it’s been really special to experience that same kindness from her personally.

In a recent development, I would say Reba. She is one of the sweetest people I’ve ever known, and in my early, early years — and still to this day — if I see her, she’s just incredibly kind and supportive. I would definitely have to say she kind of tops my list. We did a Dr. Pepper commercial together in my early 2000s and she has always been someone who uplifts everyone around her, including myself. I just love her to death. I can’t say enough good things about her.

According to recent reports, I’ve always looked up to Hilary Duff, and she was actually my very first concert! Even though she grew up in the spotlight as a child star, she has always kept a strong head on her shoulders and remained true to herself. I love her message of ‘strong, not skinny’ and the way she continues to promote confidence, self-love and a healthy perspective on body image.

I’m thankful for Stevie Nicks. I’ve always been drawn to women who create an entire world around their music, and Stevie is the ultimate example. Her songs are romantic, haunting, feminine and fierce all at once. What inspires me most at this chapter in my life is how unapologetically herself she has remained. She reminds me that there’s power in your individuality, beauty in your scars and that a woman’s creative spirit only gets more interesting with time.

Industry observers note that we are thankful for Jeffrey Steele. There’s something extra special about someone who believed in you back when you were just two guys chasing a dream. Jeffrey has been that person for us, mentoring us through the ups and downs of this industry. We wouldn’t be where we are today without him.

I’m thankful for Tim McGraw and the example he has set for us as a band. His commitment to continuing his legacy through music and touring, while prioritizing his wife and three daughters, is such a beautiful picture of a successful work-life balance. He was actually one of the first to invite us out on a big run, and hopping on his stadium tour this summer was something special. We also were so honored to surprise him during his induction into the Country Music Hall of Fame this year with our take on “Live Like You Were Dying.” He is so passionate about pouring into other artists, and having Tim be a mentor and friend all these years now means so much.

I’m thankful to Vince Gill because he was the very first person who agreed to sing on my very first album, and I hadn’t even met him yet. This act of generosity has taught me to pay it forward with other artists or songwriters. He also told me that using wedges over in ear monitors allowed for the experience of being immersed in music fully. Nashville is the foundation for my songwriting. I’m so deeply grateful for this community.

I’m thankful for Dolly because her talent and legacy have shown me so much. When I was 16, I convinced my parents to move me to Tennessee so I could sing in the country show at Dollywood. I guess you could say I’ve always been grateful for her!

I’m a country singer with California roots, so the west is in my DNA. The Bakersfield sound changed my world. It’s always felt like home to me, and Dwight Yoakam has carried that torch.

Before I had a record deal, Dwight took a chance on me and recorded “Heart Burn” with me. That duet changed my life. Singing with one of my musical heroes was a dream come true, and I’m just as grateful for the friendship that grew out of it with Dwight, his wife Emily, and their son Dalton. Dwight has become a mentor and someone I can call when I’m trying to make sense of this crazy industry. My favorite piece of advice from him is one I still carry with me. He told me, “Go with God.”.

Industry observers note that honestly, I’m thankful for Riley Green. There’s been a full-circle story behind our relationship that has shown me grace, humility and what it means to be a true friend. It showed me that a true song wins. Songwriting is King and to treat others the way you wanna be treated.

I’ve known and loved Sheryl Crow’s music since I was a kid. But over the past two years, while writing my last record and going through a deep season of transformation, I found my way back to her albums. Songs I’d known for years took on a completely new meaning. “Strong Enough,” “My Favorite Mistake,” “Maybe Angels,” “The First Cut Is the Deepest”. It felt like I was hearing them for the first time, with enough life behind me to understand them differently.

To me, Sheryl’s music is what embodied art sounds like. There’s something so instinctive about it, like the words and melodies could move straight from whatever she was feeling into the music. You hear the ache, the humor, the desire, the contradictions. It all gets to be there.

Industry observers note that in this season of my own life, I’ve been trying to remove as many filters as I can between myself and the audience. That’s made me appreciate the openness in her music even more. It reminds me how powerful a song can be when you let someone close enough to recognize themselves in you. I can get so caught up in finding the right words that sometimes I forget to trust the real ones.

I’m forever grateful for her songs, but just as grateful for her example: the dedication to her craft, the commitment to saying things that matter, and the courage to let the truest parts of herself find a place in the music.

This year, I had the privilege of opening for Kacey Musgraves on her Middle of Nowhere tour. After meeting her and getting to know her, it is clear to me why she is as successful as she is. Not only is she incredibly talented, but she pays attention to details and is very hands-on in everything she does. I witnessed her talking to the lighting director for an hour after her sound check until they got the colors exactly the way she wanted them. She works on all levels of her career. That is how it should be, and that is something I would like to apply to my own career.

I’ll forever be thankful for my friend Keith Urban who was the first artist to take me out on the road as an opener. Watching him thrill crowds every night and run his entire tour like a well-oiled machine was a masterclass on how it’s done.

I’m thankful for Miranda Lambert because she has been supportive of me and my art from the beginning. She sends me long notes after binging my album, making me promise to keep going. She calls when she loves a song. When she asks how I’m doing, she genuinely means it. Miranda is as real and authentic as she is badass.

The fans! The way they show up for me and support me, it really inspires me to keep going and give them everything I have to give. I love The Lefties and I’m so grateful for them!

I’m thankful for Deana Carter. “Strawberry Wine” was one of my favorite songs growing up. It reminded me of my high school sweetheart back in the day. It was just such a nostalgic country song, and it’s still so good even today. I remember when I first kind of started in the country world, I told my producer how much I loved Deana Carter, and she came over and we wrote a song together, and she let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and she didn’t have to do that, and she’s so sweet and such a kind person. I still remember that. I wasn’t known at all in the country world, and she still took the time to sit with me, write a song and let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and it was a memory I’ll always remember. I’ll never forget that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s the Thanksgiving holiday weekend. Millions of people will soon be gathering with family, catching everybody up on the goings-on in their lives over the past year. A subset of those people will be gamers, who may be subject to blank stares from aunts and uncles whose conception of the multibillion-dollar industry has not progressed beyond calling every console a “Nintendo” or confused inquiries from relatives who’ve just recently been made aware that video games are a thing by all the breathless coverage of GTA 6 on network television.

Both of those people are my mom.

She has never really taken an interest in what I do, and while that stings a bit, she is at least happy that I am happy in my chosen profession and that’s good enough for me.

According to recent reports, in one of the exceedingly rare times that she has ever asked me directly about my job, she called me the other day asking if I was “excited” for the pending release of GTA 6. She used stronger language than “excited” but I’m not gonna repeat exactly what she said to me because it’s something no child should ever hear their parent say to them in any context but it involved “cream” and “drawers” so draw your own conclusions.

Industry observers note that I explained to her that 1) ew and 2) I’m not excited per se, but I am interested to see what happens with this game and how we talk about it. But I also told her that despite the sensational coverage of the game, its development price tag, and its status as the most anticipated game this decade…it’s not for me. I’ve never been into those games and I don’t see GTA 6 changing that stance much. We swiftly moved on to other topics.

According to recent reports, at first, this exchange reopened that unhealed wound of “I wish you took a greater interest in the thing I’ve built a life on.” If she had, she might know that I’m more of a Kingdom Hearts girlie, the game I used to play by ferrying my PS2 from its box under my bed to the 12-inch tube TV in her room when I was 16 years old. But as I think about it now, even though she’s wildly missed the mark on my tastes and preferences, I actually really appreciate that she asked at all. She saw a video game on TV and thought, “Oh hey, my daughter does video games, let me talk to her about that.” That was her attempt at connecting with me, and it’s way more than a lot of other parents do when it comes to engaging with their children’s passion professions, so thanks, mom.

You, too, might be a person who has a gamer in your life who you’ll have the chance to catch up with this holiday weekend. And while there’s a very good chance that, unlike me, they’re actually into GTA 6, here’s a quick list of topics to broach just in case they’re not.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, in the movie about the founding and success of Hershey’s chocolate, Alexandra Daddario plays Milton Hershey’s wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey.
  • It was fantastic, and it was interesting to see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We talk a lot about Alexandra Daddario’s style and her knack for hopping on trends like the little black dress and corsets. She’s also been open about her costumes for movies. For example, she’s talked a lot about wearing that iconic red swimsuit for Baywatch. Now, in her newest film, Hershey, she had to wear lots of corsets. When I asked her about that and the stunning period dresses she wore in this film, she told me why they were “fantastic.”.

According to recent reports, in the movie about the founding and success of Hershey’s chocolate, Alexandra Daddario plays Milton Hershey’s wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey. The film covers a lot of Hershey’s life, from growing up in the late mid to late-1800s to the later years of his life in the mid-1900s. That means it spans the entirety of Milton and Kitty’s relationship. So, for the various decades represented in the project on the 2026 movie schedule, Daddario had different corsets to wear, as she explained:.

It was fantastic, and it was interesting to see. You know, they were like historians in costumes. And I didn't realize that there were different kinds of corsets for different decades, different time periods, I should say. So we had different corsets as Kitty gets older, and that was interesting and helped me get into character.

I can totally see how the corsets helped Daddario. While painful at times, they alter how you carry yourself. So, I’d imagine that having different ones for different times in her character's life helped her figure out how to stand, move around and evolve Kitty’s physicality.

Milton and Kitty were married from 1898 to 1915, when Kitty died. So, in Hershey we get to see their meet-cute, and Daddario wearing a gorgeous pink corseted dress and floral hat. We also see their final days together. It’s an emotional tale, and as their relationship evolves, so does Kitty’s fashion (and corsets).

Now, when I asked The White Lotus actress about her favorite outfit, she said she couldn’t pick a specific one. However, she did call out another element of her costumes that helped her get into character:.

Recent findings suggest that they were all so beautiful and great. I love the hats; they were just so out there. And she, Kitty, wore these incredible hats. So that really helped me get into character and have some fun.

I love how much these looks helped her get into character. As someone who has been a fan of Alexandra Daddario’s fashion game for years, I was looking forward to speaking with her about her outfits in Hershey, because they stand out so much. They’re beautiful and fitting for the time, and I think it’s so cool that they really helped the actress find her character.

Now, if you’d like to see Alexandra Daddario as Kitty, you can catch Hershey in theaters now.

Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry has announced it will host a 'Cherry Time Special Presentation' on 27th November, bringing more information to light about the game's first significant DLC offering, Sea of Sorrows. We know that the free update will be nautically-themed - hence the eponymous 'sea' - and will feature fresh bosses, areas and so on, but other than that, information about what's coming is vague.

But it seems that's not all; as well as more information about the mysterious patch to the hit Metroidvania game, the studio has also unveiled "a bunch" of other "exciting announcements." Curious.

It has been revealed that the Cherry Time Special Presentation will kick off at 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm GMT / 4pm CEST. I'll embed the video below, so check back here at the time if you need a bookmark.

Recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. Whilst these editions contained mostly expected information, there was an unforeseen mention of "free content packs" that would be arriving alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC. Will we hear more about these as part of this newly introduced showcase? We don't have too long to find out.

It seems likely, though. "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with latest friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" Team Cherry has repeatedly confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support, but other than this upcoming DLC, we don't really know what that entails.

Additionally, Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - will we see it shadowdrop as part of this stream? Stranger things have happened, especially in the world of Hollow Knight….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's Thanksgiving weekend, so what better time is there to kick back and relax after a good meal with a new movie or TV show? However, if the thought of combing through all of the many streaming platforms fills you with dread, that's where we come in. We've compiled the ultimate list for what you can stream this weekend, including new movies arriving on streaming, original releases, and the finale to one of our favorite shows.

So whether you're after sci-fi and fantasy, like the newly introduced Blade Runner show, or you're in the mood for an epic war movie, like The Mosquito Bowl, then we've got something for everyone. In our list below, we go through each of the major streaming services pulling out all of the best things you can watch this week.

Industry observers note that we don't include any new digital releases for purchase on this list either so as long as you have a subscription, everything below is completely free. This gives you more loose change for your Black Friday purchases too.

As a quick note, we haven't got any HBO Max recommendations this week so check out our guides to the best HBO Max shows and the best HBO Max movies for what to watch there.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Prime Video.

Blade Runner 2099 tells a newly introduced story set in the beloved franchise, some 50 years on from when we last entered the neon-streaked sci-fi world. It's a very different setting this time around too as replicants have now taken power following an uprising. In this harsh landscape, Cora (played by Hunter Schafer) forms an unlikely pairing with a dying replicant called Olwen (Michelle Yeoh).

According to recent reports, across the eight-part drama, the pair try to track down a runaway who is harboring a truth that could collapse their fragile city. Reviews have been pretty positive for this one with plenty of praise for the impressive worldbuilding. All eight episodes are out now as well, making the perfect binge-watch for this holiday weekend. Once you've watched the whole season, be sure to check out our Blade Runner 2099 ending explained and our guide to the Blade Runner timeline.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

For more, here's our list of the best movies on Prime Video.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Netflix.

It has been revealed that bill Skarsgård and Nicholas Galitzine lead this latest Netflix war drama from Friday Night Lights helmer Peter Berg. Based on the non-fiction novel of the same name, the movie follows four American college football players who enlist together in the marines during World War Two following the attack on Pearl Harbor.

Industry observers note that as well as charting their lives and their experiences on the battlefield, the film focuses on the iconic football game that was played before the Battle of Okinawa, a fascinating part of military history. Emotional and uplifting in equal measures, it's an epic story that's available to stream right now.

Want more to watch? Here's our guide to the best movies on Netflix.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Prime Video.

The final two episodes of Amazon's fantasy epic The Rings of Power season 3 are available to stream right now. In episode 7, we get to witness the crafting of the One Ring for the first time on screen, an epic sequence that any Tolkien fan will rejoice at. Then the finale sets up perfectly where the show will be heading next in the just-confirmed The Rings of Power season 4.

In a recent development, with some time over the holiday weekend, it's the perfect moment to catch up on The Lord of the Rings prequel, especially given the show's unusual release structure. In our The Rings of Power season 3 review we praised the scale of the series that seems to be getting better with every season. Head to Middle-earth this weekend and check it out.

Here's our pick of the best shows on Prime Video to watch right now.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Apple TV.

Marvel star Chris Pratt returns to the screen in this heartwarming movie about a Navy SEAL who trains his nephew how to become a "warrior kid" before he enters high school. Dealing with an injury that rules him out of serving, he focuses all his attention and military training to help out the youngster in this comedy from Charlie's Angels and Terminator Salvation director McG.

Based on a children's novel of the same name, it's a light-hearted bit of escapism to enjoy this weekend. The movie hasn't blown critics away but audiences on Rotten Tomatoes have already been scoring the film much higher, landing an 86% rating at the time of writing. Not bad at all.

We've also got a list of the best movies on Apple TV.

Available: USWhere to watch: Hulu.

After arriving in theaters earlier this year, this Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson starrer finally arrives on Hulu. It follows a former soldier played by Ritchson as he is thrown into a brutal race against time with Wilson's courier to try and deliver a liver to a dying young girl. In their way is a ruthless cartel who will stop at nothing to secure the organ.

According to recent reports, plenty of action, comedy, and an unlikely buddy pairing, the movie comes from former stunt performer Scott Waugh, who previously helmed Expend4bles. Generally positive reviews praised the lead duo's performances and the epic scale of the action, making this our pick for one of the best newly introduced movies to stream this weekend.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they rapidly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level.
  • Sources indicate that the enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations.
  • So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they rapidly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level. Sadly, with a sudden hotfix last night, this particular use case for the enchant has been removed.

Sources indicate that the enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations. What it does is simple: when you fail to deal a critical strike with a spell, the next spell hit is guaranteed to do so. What made this particularly powerful is that the buff also worked with continuous area of effect spells, meaning an early instance of the spell not crit-ing would result in the remaining damage hits all dealing critical damage.

So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell. This is a channel spell with a total of 10 seconds of cast time. Every second, it deals damage. If the first instance of damage at the one second mark doesn't crit, the remaining nine instances of damage would all crit. This resulted in absurd amounts of damage, and made players of druids, warlocks, and mages very happy.

Industry observers note that while strong enchantments are often pricey, this was notably cheap, due to the low-cost of resources used to create it and the low requirements to learn it. As such, people were spending a handful of gold for an early game enchantment that was being actively used all the way into the end game.

Industry observers note that it was admittedly a tad too strong, and the effect triggered on AOE spells was almost certainly an unintended effect of the enchantment. Last night, the fun came to an end. Now, the effect is used up as intended in long-casted spells. So going back to the example given, if the first instance of damage on Hurricane doesn't crit, then the second one still will. However, this will use up the effect, and the third instance of damage will revert to regular ol' damage numbers. It also seems as though it Revelation can't trigger more than once during a single channeled spell.

In a recent development, this is the latest in a string of ongoing quickfire bug fixes and game adjustments being made to World of Warcraft: Forever. The devs have been continuously updating the game in an attempt to curb certain gold farms, following the discovery of a particularly lucrative Blackmaw Hold gold exploit. The dev team has expressed some interesting ideas for the game longterm, including a desire to kill best-in-slot gear.

#144349. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • Industry observers note that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

Industry observers note that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

According to recent reports, dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

Industry observers note that the casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He states to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most crucial roles, including the exciting newly introduced additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

Recent findings suggest that in Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she indicates. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

According to recent reports, of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” claims Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” notes Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she states. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the massive surprises in the ensemble.”.

In a recent development, taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” indicates Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” states Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

In a recent development, pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she states. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most important for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

#144347. Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" notes head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1505 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" notes head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.
  • Our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion.
  • In a recent development, some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.

Our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion. Personally I quite like the pop-ups - I find the act of figuring out systems and how they're manipulated almost as fun as the games they're a part of. And pop-ups or no, the fact that GTA 6 can arguably be portrayed as 'rewarding' empathy and 'discouraging' the series' famous rampages of mass violence has sparked a fair bit of debate.

In a recent development, some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start. Is it incentivising and disincentivising certain in-game behaviour, or just putting a label on it? And then, actually: does the act of labelling "psycho" behaviour alone actually become a disincentivising factor in itself?

Either way, until now Rockstar hasn't mentioned a great deal about why, exactly, this system - seen by some as one that builds empathy into GTA's chaotic world - was implemented in the first place. But during an interview I had with Rob Nelson, Rockstar Games' head of development, just before GTA 6's launch earlier this month, a little more on that came to light.

Recent findings suggest that A little context is necessary here: Nelson's response was actually following a question I had about the overall approach to design that Rockstar took, and how its wider themes and intentions came about. As a part of that, he turned to this system - and how, in a way, it exists here because of the work the studio simply didn't want to leave behind after Red Dead Redemption 2.

According to recent reports, nelson explained that this all began when the team was in the early phase of exploring what type of game GTA 6 would be, in 2015 and 2016, while much of the studio was still working full-tilt on RDR2 - a game which itself didn't release until late 2018. The team was looking to "build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice than we had [before], and more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence," Nelson told me.

Recent findings suggest that the idea would be that "it's still a world of violence - but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money." Ideas that were "simple things" in principle, he remarked, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems.".

Then, as systems were gradually implemented, it became a question of "trying to marry up what you're doing in the open world with who we're saying you are in the narrative - more than we had, I would say, previously, in Red Dead 2." It's here where the system now referred to as the Criminal Profile started to form.

The thinking turned to "the nature of 'honour', which wasn't always a part of it" with Red Dead Redemption 2, Nelson continued, "but became part of it as we were working on this story and finding that the 'redemption arc' didn't feel so good when it was foisted upon you - and feelings that we had playing Red Dead sort of early on." (Those feelings, primarily, were around getting you to invest in a gang led by Dutch Van der Linde, who was fundamentally unlikable from the off - or plain "crazy", as Nelson put it. The implementation of more player choices and agency was part of Rockstar's way to build investment in Arthur, even as he followed Dutch.).

Industry observers note that that meant moving the choices away from key story moments, where many games tend to put them. Instead, Rockstar built a system that ran alongside the story via smaller, moment-to-moment choices you might make. "We tried to take all of those off the main flow and make them optional. So again, they're a choice.".

"Usually they involve some form of slight sacrifice or more effort on the part of the player," he added. The hope, then, was that you as a player would both "feel something", and ultimately also feel "you got the outcome that you deserved.".

It has been revealed that that was the initial thinking behind this kind of system as a whole. Coming to GTA 6, it then combined with a wider desire to "evolve" Grand Theft Auto as both the team's storytelling and the available technology matured. "You're thinking about story and character set, but we're also thinking about what we want to do with GTA as a series, and how you want to evolve it," Nelson said.

Recent findings suggest that "I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different newly introduced questions," he continued. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

"It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about," he continued. That tied back into the more sophisticated NPCs and reactions the team were making.

Recent findings suggest that "If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," he said. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?

"The team then started thinking of ways to build a bit more sustained enjoyment from it. "What if you can't do that?" Nelson continued. What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, "you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

In a recent development, "And then, he continued, "you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically claims 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

That Irredeemable profile level, for what it's worth, was another element born of Red Dead Redemption 2. "We had that with Red Dead, where people would sort of have low honour, and then 'greet' their way back up to high honour. And so this was an attempt of sorts of [making something] for people that just want to go crazy and almost opt out of the system. They can opt out of it - and you can also turn off the notifications in the system.".

It's notable, in fact, just how interlinked the thinking was with GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2. As Nelson put it at one point: "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had had, certainly in a GTA before. So we liked that idea." What Rockstar did with GTA 6 was then in a way a natural next step. "We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

We'll have much more like this from our interview with Nelson very soon, so do look out for that on Eurogamer over the coming days. In the meantime, we've a handy guide explaining exactly how GTA 6's Criminal Profile system works and how to change, raise, or lower that profile if you're in need of a deep dive into how it all really works.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 was subject to more than a few leaks in the run-up to its eventual launch, but despite it all, one significant early-game twist was kept a total secret until release – something Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson was "praying" for.

It has been revealed that before we get into it, we're obviously about to discuss some spoilers for GTA 6 Chapter 1. It's an early moment – one you'll have seen if you've played the first hour of the game – but if you're yet to dive in, you might want to bookmark this to come back to later. Or, of course, feel free to carry on if you don't care about a spoiler-free experience.

It has been revealed that everyone still here who wants to be? Great. As you probably guessed, the twist in question is the existence of Jason and Lucia's son, Tomás.

Recent findings suggest that after being moved to her aunt's care following her arrest, as shown in the game's prologue, Lucia's primary motivation is to get Tomás back and give him a good life alongside Jason, but none of this was revealed prior to launch – officially or otherwise. This was something that co-studio head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, had his "fingers crossed" for.

In an interview with VGC a few days before GTA 6's launch, Nelson confirmed that Rockstar was "never" planning to reveal the twist and, at the time, was still praying no one would spill the beans ahead of schedule. "I am still holding on," he noted. "Fingers crossed, how many more days? I'm praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we've gone through, every day I'm just like, 'please, please don't do that, please don't do that.'".

While VGC notes that there was a small amount of chatter on forums about Jason and Lucia having a son, these whispers generally didn't stick, and, notably, none of the Cyberleek videos that appeared online before launch indicated Tomás. Honestly, that feels somewhat miraculous given how early he's revealed and how frequently he comes up in the story and dialogue.

Cyberleek wasn't the only hacker to target Rockstar, either – there was also an enormous wave of GTA 6 leaks in 2022 – but even so, no baby boy and the driving force of the plot were plastered all over the internet as a result.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Anyway, however the bullet was dodged, it made for an excellent twist, and let Rockstar have the story moment it was hoping for. "It's meant to shock," Nelson explained. "We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason's character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that one of my favorite video games is Control.
  • Recent findings suggest that as reported by The Latest York Times, last month the USFS published a few documents and reports related to Bigfoot as part of a Freedom of Information request.
  • Recent findings suggest that first, a 1982 report written by someone who was sent out to study alleged Bigfoot tracks found in Mill Creek, Oregon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BigfootControlControl ResonantCreepy.

Industry observers note that one of my favorite video games is Control. I also like this year’s Control Resonant, but not quite as much. And one of the best parts of those games is the government reports and files documenting creepy happenings and events in the game’s universe. Meanwhile, here in real life, the United States Forest Service has recently released some files about Bigfoot, and I was very pleased to see that feel like they fell right out of Control.

Recent findings suggest that as reported by The Latest York Times, last month the USFS published a few documents and reports related to Bigfoot as part of a Freedom of Information request. One file is just a clipping of a newspaper article from a Montana newspaper in the ’80s about substantial, strange footprints found in the snow. The other two are far more interesting.

Recent findings suggest that first, a 1982 report written by someone who was sent out to study alleged Bigfoot tracks found in Mill Creek, Oregon. Look at this and tell me it doesn’t look and read like something you’d pick up in Control.

In a recent development, the report goes over, in a lot of detail, the footprints that were spotted. Ultimately, the report’s conclusion was that these tracks were fake, with the writer citing inconsistencies with gait pattern, signs of tampering with leaves, and other pieces of evidence that led them to conclude the tracks were “made by something other than a 300-pound plus two-footed being.”.

The other piece of Bigfoot documentation released by the USFS is what appears to be a short document written by someone who really thought Petty Creek, Montana was special and historically notable. One reason it was historically important: Bigfoot, baby. Here’s the bit about a Bigfoot sighting that allegedly happened in the ’40s.

Another type creature that walked on its hind legs, that altho there wasn’t actual sightings, tracks, a strong odor, and a grunting sound were observed. The first time was when four of us went in to pack out a six point bull elk on our backs and on arriving where the elk was supposed to be laying we found the intrails only and in the snow coming to and leading away from the area was a large set of tracks. At first we guessed it was a very large bear except bears don’t walk on their hind legs only for short distances and ordinarily would drag a carcass this large.

Industry observers note that this event took place in 1949 in the South fork of Petty cr. about where the present Garden point road goes. The following year when W.W. Schmitz was hunting in the upper Bills creek area he came across the same type of tracks and smelled a strong odor and heard a grunting type noise. He decided that he could find elk elsewhere and left the area. At this time we had never heard of Bigfoot so passed it off as something we didn’t want anything to do with and let it go at that.

The whole thing was typed up on a typewriter and even contains a bit of extra text at the bottom, written afterwards by hand. All of this, including the official seals, the black-and-white photos, and the matter-of-fact writing in the official report, feels like stuff I’d read in Control right before encountering Bigfoot. Sadly, it’s unlikely a substantial ape stalks the woods of the United States. But it’s fun to read about it, you know?

GTA 6's head of production told me that they have the team and resources to include oddities, paranormal moments, and weird monsters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunting Wives has been renewed for season 3 — but fans might not see every cast member returning to the show.

In a recent development, based on May Cobb‘s book of the same name, The Hunting Wives introduced Sophie (Brittany Snow), who found herself drawn to prominent socialite Margo (Malin Åkerman) after moving from Boston to an East Texas town. While some became invested in the murder at the center of the series, the show’s first season also provided plenty of entertainment with guns, drinking and steamy onscreen hookups.

Recent findings suggest that despite the obstacles facing Sophie and Margo, Åkerman hasn’t given up hope on the pair’s future. “They find a way,” she told Us in November 2026 ahead of the season 2 premiere. “They come together and they break apart. It’s the epic, toxic love story that we all adore, so that’s really up to [creator] Rebecca [Cutter] to decide how they eventually, by season 13, run off together and live happily ever after.”.

Åkerman jokingly agreed that things would be easier for them with some men out of the way.

Recent findings suggest that “I agree [that we need to get rid of the men]. We need to because we need to get them out of the way so Sophie and Margo can be together forever,” she said. “And [Margo’s husband] Jed is standing in the way right now. But it’d be tricky.”.

It has been revealed that cutter also spoke to Us about the odds of a happy ending for the couple, saying, “Sophie obviously is the eyes through which we see the show. When she came in, she wasn’t ready for a Margo Banks. She wanted it, but she was in a weakened place in her life.”.

In a recent development, she continued: “Over the course of two seasons, she becomes formidable. She becomes fierce. She becomes worthy and equal [to] Margo. So I think their relationship does get real in season 2, and we have moments, though, where we can really imagine a Margo and Sophie happy ending for them. But of course, they’re both survivors, and that trumps everything.”.

Here are our PS Plus monthly games for December 2026

💡 Key Takeaways

There's a chill in the air and a snowman (plastic) at the end of the street, meaning winter is firmly upon us. So what better way to make it way through the long dark nights than a spot of festmas gaming. And hark, just in the nick of time, PlayStation Plus' monthly games for December have been revealed, with some skating, spooking, and dragon baubles.

In a recent development, not the most festive bunch, then, but some decent stuff all the same. Amnesia: The Bunker is a real winner if you like it spooky (and The Bunker is very spooky), setting players loose in a labyrinthine underground WW1 bunker where something awful prowls. It's a "truly unsettling adventure" as we wrote in our Amnesia: The Bunker review.

As for the other two, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 is well worth your time, taking the beloved early 2000s skating games and giving them a successful modern-day makeover. We called it a "properly glorious collection of two classic games" in our Pro Skater 3+4 review. As for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, the critical consensus seems to suggest it is 'okay'.

Breaking: Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (682 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director.
  • "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, claims in an interview with Eurogamer.
  • The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, claims in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.

Recent findings suggest that "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money.".

The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that "You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically indicates, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt—but I appreciate having the option.

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” notes British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

According to recent reports, kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by Upcoming Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley notes of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

It has been revealed that “It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Industry observers note that as Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Grand Theft Auto, for obvious reasons, canât use the existing brand names that we see every day in real life.
  • The writing in theÂ GTA games has elevated and, to Rockstarâs credit, so have the fake brand names in general.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Recent findings suggest that one thing that keeps striking me about Grand Theft Auto 6 is how good the writing is, even compared to that in previous games in the series. I enjoyed those earlier games, sure, but the dialogue and storytelling in GTA 6 are a cut above the rest in terms of both the game’s compelling characters and its worldbuilding. The fact that GTAÂ is set in an analogue of the real world helps the worldbuilding bridge gaps that most fictional universes couldnât, but Iâm increasingly finding that the standout writing is fighting a war within the game itself against some of the other jokes that have been building up in the series for over a quarter century.

Grand Theft Auto, for obvious reasons, canât use the existing brand names that we see every day in real life. In this sense it’s the opposite of the Like a Dragon series, which proudly wears all its licensed brand deals on its chest and even had to write a narrative around losing the license to a key landmark in the seventh game in the series. Talking Budweiser into lending their brand name to GTA 4 would have been an uphill battle and maybe also raised some uncomfortable questions about the gameâs proximity to real-world places and events. Better to just call your in-game equivalent Pisswasser and move on.

But weâre in 2026 now. The writing in theÂ GTA games has elevated and, to Rockstarâs credit, so have the fake brand names in general. Taco Bomb is a pretty good one as a stand-in for Taco Bell. ZIP for GAP is also good. Weazel News for Fox News makes sense on a couple of different levels, Snapmatic for Instagram is something that you recognize immediately upon hearing it. But there are a handful of brand names I think the series needs to ditch, as theyâre taking away from the more interesting narratives Rockstar wants to tell.

Sources indicate that pisswasser is not a bad joke on its own, but it wears its welcome out fast. Marbles, the McDonaldâs stand-in in GTA, sells a burger called Major Balls. I get it, Big Mac, Big Balls, sure. But come on, man. Weâre scraping the bottom of the barrel here. Zombix isnât even a good pun. Itâs like someone filed that one in the ten minutes before the deadline. We need to start thinking intelligently about which of these benefit worldbuilding and which detract from it.

I’m not saying all of these need to go or even a majority of them. There are plenty of good joke brand names, but there are also ones that are very, very 2000s, and it would be better for the games if they disappear. Grand Theft Auto has grown with its audience, and it’s now delivering narratives that genuinely keep up with well-written modern movies, so why are we limiting aspects of it to jokes that would appear in an Epic Movie parody?

Rockstar can and should start taking a look at these and see what makes sense for their games every so often. Audit the world, donât just assume that because it existed in previous games, it needs to exist forever.

Itâs not like brands donât just disappear from the real world all the time. Joannâs Fabrics isnât around anymore, but your world keeps spinning, just like it would if the Obey car line simply did not appear in a latest game. You planning to take a Spirit Airlines flight this holiday? Youâre sure as hell not, nor would you be a sobbing mess on the floor if a Big Balls sandwich billboard wasnât overlooking a highway chase.

Sources indicate that there are already so many good jokes in these games that the lame ones can get cut out without losing anything. No one is wrong for liking them, but maybe the games themselves can be better for examining what works and what doesnât. No series has ever escaped a need for refreshing itself and iterating over the years and, in almost every way, GTA 6 nails it. Thereâs just one more thing I want to see them look at before they build their next GTA world, asking themselves if each jokey brand name still fits their vision. If it does, great! If they decide it would be better to snip, that would be fine, too.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA Sports FC 27 is using gen-AI to digitally recreate the voice of veteran football commentator John Motson - the FIFA video game series' first ever real-world announcer who died in 2023.
  • Recent findings suggest that john Motson commentated on hundreds of football games over the course of five different decades, starting in the 1970s.
  • But EA's now decided to digitally resurrect Motson - or, at least, his incredibly recognisable voice - with permission from his family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports FC 27 is using gen-AI to digitally recreate the voice of veteran football commentator John Motson - the FIFA video game series' first ever real-world announcer who died in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that john Motson commentated on hundreds of football games over the course of five different decades, starting in the 1970s. The English commentator then became the mainstay voice of EA's dominant football simulation series, beginning with FIFA 96 all the way up until FIFA 2005, when the publisher decided to go in a different direction.

But EA's now decided to digitally resurrect Motson - or, at least, his incredibly recognisable voice - with permission from his family. An update with Motson's voice will go live on 26th November. "There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board," senior game designer director Mat Prior noted in a statement given to the BBC earlier today.

"At the outset we wanted to pay tribute to to Motty as the commentator and as this emotional connection - he was the very first voice of our game - so we really wanted to do him justice and bring him back," Prior added, explaining that Motson's posthumous role in the game is being handled with a mixture of previously recorded voice lines and AI. EA supposedly went down the AI route since it doesn't have recordings of Motson commentating over newer, more fresh faced footballers.

Fred Motson said it "means an awful lot" to hear his dad's voice in the game again, and he reckons his dad was "always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects," even if he wasn't the most technologically savvy person. EA said it had paid the family for the rights to use Motson's voice and likeness.

Save Our Voices Now founder Peter Caulfield - who campaigns for the government to regulate the use of generative AI voice cloning tech - told the BBC he wasn't comfortable with the project. "In life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," he noted. "Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." He doesn't have a problem with actors consenting to AI voice replication while they're still alive, however.

A Japanese acting union recently fought back against this very same practice by proposing new guidelines that would stop the replication of dead actors' voices without their permission.

Generative AI has been widely controversial in the games industry for other reasons, too. In recent months, there's been a huge impact on smaller game developers who are worried that their games could be cloned by AI copycats and some who have had to delay their release dates because of Steam's growing approvals backlog.

Recent findings suggest that "The Grounds comes across as a frippery, Ultimate Team rumbles ever on, but FC 27 brings meaningful changes to the fluidity and speed of play. Given that its practical football-game monopoly is more or less unchallenged, EA could do a lot less than this," Josh Wise wrote in Eurogamer's EA Sports FC 27 review.

Luke Wilson reflected on the legacy of The Family Stone in the midst of shooting next year’s highly-anticipated sequel.

In a recent development, “I feel like I’ve just kind of been in a bubble making it here for the last month,” Wilson, 55, exclusively told Us via his partnership with Fanatics. “It was one of those movies where, you know, it was really fun to make the first one. A great group of people. It came out and people seemed to like it. But then it was a few years later, I’d start to hear things like, ‘Oh my family and I watch that every Thanksgiving,’ or ‘My family and I watch that every Christmas.’ Each year it seemed like more.”.

The actor added, “I’m so used to Chevy Chase and Christmas Vacation or It’s a Wonderful Life. So when people started to say their families were watching The Family Stone, I said, ‘Really?’ But now it does seem like it’s become a genuine tradition for people.”.

The Family Stone was released in 2005, featuring an ensemble cast including Rachel McAdams, Dermot Mulroney, Sarah Jessica Parker, Claire Danes, Craig T. Nelson and the late Diane Keaton. A sequel was unveiled in September with all of the original cast set to return, plus the addition of 9-time Emmy winner, Jean Smart.

Sources indicate that “I’m wary of saying anything about the damn plot because I feel like I’d have the studio come down on my head,” Wilson joked. “I’ll just say people get together, people split apart, babies are born. It revolves around Christmas again and I think it comes out in November of next year.”.

Wilson plays Ben Stone — sibling of Everett (Mulroney), Amy (McAdams), Susannah (Elizabeth Reaser) and Thad (Ty Giordano) — who ultimately ends up with Meredith (Parker) at the end of the first movie.

While Wilson was understandably coy about what to expect from the sequel itself, he gushed about the experience of reuniting with the cast.

It has been revealed that “I’ve never gone back to the same characters, the same group of people,” Wilson explained. “It’s been really fun. Just to be around Sarah Jessica, who was so great to work with. She kind of helped put the movie together.”.

Sources indicate that he added, “It’s been great to be around Craig T. Nelson. He’s been really funny. He’ll just be like, ‘What are we doing, man? Why are we here? Why am I here?’ But it’s been a good feeling.”.

According to recent reports, in addition to returning to The Family Stone, Wilson is the face of Fanatics’ Town Hall, the brand’s season-long NFL campaign. The campaign features Wilson alongside former NFL great Calvin Johnson and former LSU gymnast and influencer Livvy Dunne, celebrating the passion of NFL fans and highlighting FanCash, Fanatics’ universal rewards currency.
