📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that my elderly mom, who has been deeply unwell for a number of years, has recently started clenching her hands into balls and curling her feet inward like little hooks. Her gerontologist said that, horribly enough, her mind is no longer sending a message to her body that she needs to relax. Medicine can’t help, she explained, but massage might. So one evening, I turned to Google Maps, where I increasingly find everything from authentic Thai restaurants to the best place to buy youth soccer cleats. I guided the map app to the Upper West Side, one of the country’s most expensive neighborhoods, and put one word in the search bar: “massage.”.

Then I squinted. Why was the massage table at “Ashley massage and spa” lit by dark purple light? And why did another listing have photos of the masseuse herself in skin-tight exercise wear, with directions to contact her on Telegram? But it all became clearer when I spotted a description of the type of massage services offered: “I’m available for deep tissue, Swedish, or any kind of massage appointment with a happy ending.”.

In a recent development, even if nothing should surprise us anymore about our tech overlords, I was still pretty shocked to find that Google Maps appeared to be the fresh Craigslist, famous for its battle with regulators over sex work classifieds. Somewhere between figuring out the location of the neighborhood CVS and “coffee near me,” it seems like Google branched out. I’d always assumed it adhered to local laws—sex work is illegal in New York state—but perhaps Silicon Valley’s fave “we’re just a platform not a publisher” defense applied here. Otherwise, why on earth was the algorithm retrieving sex work listings when I was just trying to help my 84-year-old mom?

I emailed Google PR to ask what, exactly, was going on, giving them a deadline of the next day to respond.

Recent findings suggest that the response came from a senior publicist, quickly. “Hi Vanessa - I'm on the Google Comms team. Would you be able to provide the listings and screenshots?”.

I did so, then received another response: “I’m reviewing all of this, but wondering if you have wiggle room in your deadline? Want to make sure I can get you the right info in time, and I think that timing tomorrow may be challenging.”.

I responded that I could wait until a couple more days to find out what Google had to say.

In the meantime, I contacted some experts.

In a recent development, mike Blumenthal has been studying Google Maps almost since it existed. A co-founder of Near Media, he began writing about the product in 2005 and says he first documented large-scale spam on Maps in Latest York City in 2009. When I showed him the strange massage listings I’d found scattered across New York, he wasn’t particularly surprised. Google Maps is an extraordinarily valuable way to get in front of customers, which gives gray and black market businesses a powerful incentive to game it. Once they figure out how to convince Google’s algorithm that real people should be directed to those listings, “they can make bank.”.

In a recent development, google removes an enormous amount of fake listings, reviews and images, and has tightened its verification procedures over the years, stated Blumenthal. But when those systems fail, enforcement is largely reactive. Even Blumenthal, who has volunteered in Google’s forums for nineteen years and knows how to escalate a complaint, said getting suspicious listings removed can take upwards of a month or six weeks. When a problem attracts press attention, though, he says Google can act within hours. What Google doesn’t do, in his view, is spend enough to prevent the same problems from recurring. “They won’t put in place systemic fixes. They won’t put in place people to deal with this quickly…They don’t want the cost.”.

Sources indicate that after I talked to Blumenthal, I read the reviews of some of the massage businesses that Google Maps was serving up nationwide. Not all were positive. One reviewer of the “Asian Palace Spa” in San Francisco, writing five years ago, gave the business one star and called it a “fraud,” saying he had paid for an hour-long massage but received only 15 minutes before being asked for additional money for “extra services.” The review had received 17 likes. Another one-star reviewer from the same period remarked, “they don’t have spa, just pay for room and then pay for lady for whatever you do.”.

In a recent development, but many more of the illicit massage businesses had positive reviews, about services that were above and beyond, with smiley kissy face icons attached. Were these just independent sex workers trying to make a living? Was it so wrong that they were using Google Maps to find clients? Perhaps it’s needless to say, but when I called several of the phone numbers and introduced myself as a reporter, information was not forthcoming.

In a recent development, I started to feel a little queasy as I reviewed a listing that was clearly written by a woman working for herself, just trying to make a listing. But then, as I looked more closely at others, I realized that the photos were so similar, and the setups of the listings so close to each other, that they must be coordinated by an organized group. Whether that was a lead-generator for escorts who needed extra clients, or a scammer, or a sex trafficker, I couldn’t tell.

It has been revealed that I searched for illicit massage listings in different cities, and found them all over neighborhoods in Los Angeles, from Beverly Hills to Koreatown. I also began to notice that most of the massage spots seemed as though they were unlikely to actually be located in the spots they claimed to be. For example, a masseuse who appeared to be nude from breastbone up, with a butterfly tattoo decorating her clavicle, located her business on the Upper East Side’s Museum Mile, home to multimillion dollar apartments and New York’s great cultural institutions, but she also included information about a certain corner in Queens, where it seemed like she could’ve also set up shop.

Now that I had more information, I tried to understand whether Google Maps bore any responsibility for these listings, calling Chelsea Binns, a professor at John Jay College of Criminal Justice who studies cybercrime. “It’s interesting from an anti-fraud perspective, because we rely on Google Maps virtually every day now,” she said, taking the call from Japan. “No one takes out a hard map anymore. And there’s a bit of borrowed credibility, because these listings are on Google. It’s Google Maps!”.

According to recent reports, despite this, Binns says responsibility rests with each individual user to decipher the legitimacy of a Google Maps business, a caveat emptor situation. “A lot of us don’t read disclaimers, but somewhere deep within the service it says they’re not at fault,” explains Binns. “It’s ‘use at your own risk, research independently, and verify.’”.

“But why don’t they care if it’s an illegal service?” I ask. “They wouldn’t have guns on there.”.

According to recent reports, “They do care,” notes Binns. “They actively review their content. I suspect this slipped through the cracks. But at some point you’re just playing whack-a-mole. You take one down, and another pops up.”.

This was the perspective of AI-critic Brian Merchant, creator of the Blood in the Machine podcast and newsletter. “As [Google] has moved their resources into moderating, training, and shipping AI, I would not be surprised if resources that were dedicated to moderating are falling off, and things are just staying up longer,” he claims. “And maybe criminal organizations have been emboldened, realizing that they can get their links listed higher and longer, and it’ll be weeks before they’re taken down.”.

Industry observers note that but the next time I checked out the massage listings near my mom’s apartment, almost all had disappeared. And I heard back from Google with a statement: “Google Maps only displays places that people can visit or interact with in the real world, and we've removed the businesses that do not exist at these locations.”.

Recent findings suggest that this seemed to indicate that Google had taken action to remove listings in my mom’s neighborhood, and that I was also correct when I noticed that some of the sex workers weren’t actually in the locations they said they were. Google also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

A Google spokesperson further pushed back against Mike Blumenthal’s contention that the firm doesn’t want to incur costs monitoring Google Maps, noting, “we placed posting restrictions on more than 782,000 policy-violating accounts and removed over 13 million fake Business Profiles, further defending genuine businesses on Maps. We blocked or removed over 292 million policy-violating reviews, while publishing more than 1 billion helpful reviews.” Google also added, “we hold bad actors accountable through account suspension and litigation. We display alerts to let you know if we've recently removed suspicious five-star reviews in certain circumstances. These warnings help you understand quickly if a place may be engaging in unfair review practices.”.

They also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

According to recent reports, I contacted Danielle Citron, a professor at the University of Virginia School of Law, to understand more. She said that Google’s statement made sense. “Ordering, filtering, and otherwise structuring the presentation of content” is likely to be shielded as “publishing and speaking” under Section 230, the law that protects tech platforms from liability for user-uploaded content, she said. But there could be a wrinkle. “A different question is getting paid for and designing systems in a particular way, [which] may not be immunized,” she explains, mentioning social media cases like New Mexico v. Meta, “where [a lawsuit challenging platform design] was permitted to go to trial because it was about what Meta did in their design of sites, not what consumers did to kids.” So a question could potentially be asked by attorneys in the future along these lines: Is the very structure of Google Maps allowing gray and black market businesses to flourish?

Industry observers note that within a week, some listings that Google removed when I last checked seemed to have popped up in Fresh York again, but there were far less of them. Still, I found it confounding that in trying to find a massage for my mom, I had uncovered a network of massage spots that a less savvy consumer than myself might have imagined were legitimate. “We really need a better understanding of this landscape, because we need to look out for the consumer,” Binns told me. “Your mom is someone who is vulnerable in society, and that can take many forms. She’s perhaps incapable of doing the due diligence that’s required just to get an ordinary service.”.

At the same time, I was aware that no one wants to change Google’s algorithm to the point that it screws over legitimate small businesses that rely on the visibility of Google Maps. Blumenthal explained the conundrum to me this way: if Google tightens their mapping search controls too much, “businesses’ reality becomes worse, because you can’t get into [Maps]. If they loosen it, consumers’ reality becomes worse, because shit gets in.”.

Sources indicate that after all of this back and forth, I still had to solve my initial problem: securing a massage for my mom. I contacted a few spots in her neighborhood that looked legitimate, but they said she’d have to raise herself on the massage table, which, since she’s in a wheelchair, wouldn’t work. I decided to reach out to her Medicare-supplied occupational therapist, who got back to me right away.

He remarked he’d been meaning to call. He needed to send me a form saying that my mom was no longer able to participate in the exercises they were performing together, and she’d likely be kicked off Medicare payment for them in the near future. That was a bummer, and made me regret calling him at all, but I figured while I had him on the line I’d ask another question: Does Medicare (original, parts A & B) cover therapeutic massage? He said no, apologetically.

I’d spent a week investigating a system that made it remarkably easy to sell massages that weren't massages, only to discover how difficult it was to obtain one that was.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

It has been revealed that your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

Industry observers note that EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

In a recent development, hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

Industry observers note that if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

Sources indicate that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

According to recent reports, everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

You cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

According to recent reports, much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

Recent findings suggest that I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

Yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

But as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

According to recent reports, so on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

According to recent reports, but even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time issue, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

Recent findings suggest that I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a big plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. But given all the crime I’ve been doing, somehow I feel that a happy and normal future will, like the many, many restaurants of Leonida, be forever closed to them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the original Dawn of War's Winter Assault expansion added campaigns that let you play two factions at once, with different final missions based on which one you triumphed with. Dawn of War 2's campaign was even more player-led, with distress calls that had different outcomes based on what you prioritized and, in the Chaos Rising expansion, a morality mechanic with Corruption and Redemption points. It even chose a different character to be a traitor based on who gained the most Corruption by the story's end.

According to recent reports, I asked John French, Dawn of War 4's writer and a Warhammer novelist, whether Dawn of War 4 would follow this noble tradition by having player decisions alter the plot. "The player's decisions very much change the perspectives that they'll experience the game from," he replied. "So, depending on which heroes from each faction they choose, they'll have a very different experience of the game, in that they'll see different parts of the story and sometimes different views on the same events.".

Based on what we've seen of the Ork and Adeptus Mechanicus campaigns, that means partway through you'll be presented with a choice between two Commanders who have opposed goals and the one you pick will lead to missions with different objectives. Ork Beastboss Guzcutta is trying to unite his clan, the Snakebites, while his rival warboss, Gorgutz, is an off-world interloper trying to rebuild his damaged invasion force.

"With characters like Gorgutz and Guzcutta," French explained, "it can be as simple as one of them wants to do it the traditional, brutal ork way, and one of them wants to do it in a brutal but cunning way, so you have missions that focus on getting lots of shiny kit in one, while the other tries to get as many orks to follow them as possible.

Recent findings suggest that "In a more complex narrative, like the Adeptus Mechanicus campaign, Potentia-Delta-9's main drive is the quest for knowledge, and she is on a very different path from Skitarii Marshal Sek-Ix-23, who is very much about enforcing the orthodoxy. The story for both overlaps, but which character you choose and what decisions you make with them lead down different experiences of an overlapping story.".

Sources indicate that writing an RTS isn't all about plotting out the campaign missions. The Dawn of War games are legendary for their unit barks, like the saber-rattling Lord Commissar who shouts, from the top of an armored Chimera transport, "Drive me closer, I want to hit them with my sword!" Getting across so much personality in a short space is a real skill.

According to recent reports, "You can do an awful lot with just a couple of words like 'More dakka!'," French mentioned, "that tells you a huge amount about the orks on its own. Even with factions like the necrons, the way that the lower ranks respond to the higher ones with just 'Obedience,' one word, tells how their faction works.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, part of the appeal of Warhammer is the berserk variety of its armies, each with its own highly thematic identity. You walk into a shop and see the stoic space marines alongside spiky Chaos daemons and units of Astra Militarum who look like they stepped out of a trench in World War I before being given laser rifles.

According to recent reports, "Dawn of War 4 is deeply Warhammer in that way because it's got all of these different textures of factions and characters next to each other," French stated. "You have orks, and they are absolutely fixated on smashing everything they can in the pursuit of trying to have an even bigger fight. Then you've got the Adeptus Mechanicus, who revere machines as holy and worship the machine as god with complete sincerity and total conviction. Those two things literally exist side by side, along with alien races who have made themselves immortal by creating metal bodies with hyper advanced technology. And all of these different types of character come into conflict on one planet cut off in a sea of night—that's very Warhammer.".

Industry observers note that dawn of War 4 is due out on December 3 and will be available on Steam. Owners of the Commander Edition will get advance access and can play from November 30.

Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames, Zed Games. He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Massive Matter, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

According to recent reports, next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a newly introduced Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot, Jeff the Land Shark. While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027, priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff below, showing the completed build alongside his box art. See at The Lego Store The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his massive eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail, and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses. For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game. "Jeff brings together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C. Nielsen said in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the unpredictable strategist they meet in battle." Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers: Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies, and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • According to recent reports, in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • Industry observers note that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

According to recent reports, in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Industry observers note that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

Users on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again. #144243. Latest Update: Lucia’s Rise: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Forces Gamers to Grow Up—and Punishes Them With Narrative Consequences If They Refuse

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1852 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Lucia’s Rise: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Forces Gamers to Grow Up—and Punishes Them With Narrative Consequences If They Refuse

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto.
  • According to recent reports, this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine.
  • Recent findings suggest that but with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto. Juvenile, sexist, crass, embarrassing—people could accuse the games of being these things because the allegations were, in part, true. Beginning with 2001’s Grand Theft Auto III, the series began giving players the freedom to wreak havoc across satirical renditions of US cities. It was an amazing technical feat that only grew more impressive with each subsequent Grand Theft Auto game—and harder to appreciate the more those cities were filled with dick jokes and sex workers.

According to recent reports, this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine. What business did the tech giant have calling itself Rockstar Games if it cared what a bunch of prudes thought?

Recent findings suggest that but with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed. And the game’s staggering launch-day revenue—$3.79 billion—suggests that this change was a welcome one.

According to recent reports, rockstar has executed an astonishing about-face in Grand Theft Auto VI, choosing to build a game around a couple depicted with aching sincerity—from their car-boosting meet-cute to the desperate stickups they commit, with the player’s help. Jason Duval (played by Dylan Rourke) and Lucia Caminos (Manni L. Perez) are a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, out of options and on the run, hoping they can land a score massive enough to turn things around.

In a recent development, this earnestness is latest for Grand Theft Auto, which historically has had a deep love for pushing buttons. (Its sister series, the Western Red Dead Redemption, has less of a problem with heart-on-the-sleeve storytelling.) Lucia, especially, is new. She’s the first woman you can play as in the series, and by the transitive property, she’s also the first woman that Grand Theft Auto has ever had to take seriously. Doing so changes the entire shape of the series.

Until now, Grand Theft Auto has never really thought much of women. True, the games have never thought much of anyone; Rockstar traffics in a nihilistic comedy that lies somewhere between South Park and a Verhoeven film, a dim view of the United States where everyone sucks. But women, usually, have sucked the most. They’ve been the butts of countless jokes; in the Grand Theft Auto universe, they’ve been nags and drags and sex workers secondary to the men that the games were about. Grand Theft Auto III, a game that barely has a plot, begins with main character Clyde’s girlfriend betraying him after a heist, shooting him and calling him “small time” before running off with the take. It doesn’t get much better from there.

Industry observers note that so yes: Lucia is a huge pivot for the series, especially because Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t trust players with her right away. After a brief prologue in which a desperate stickup goes wrong, Lucia is sent to jail and players begin the game as her boyfriend Jason Duval. In addition to doing odd jobs for a small-time crime boss (Stephen Root) and hanging out with your pal (Bobby Moynihan), players have to choose: Are they going to be a good boyfriend? Rockstar Games know they might be making a substantial ask of their audience, so they slow-roll it. Before Lucia gets out of jail, the game suggests to the player, maybe fix the stairs? Or get a haircut? Buy her a necklace?

Industry observers note that in the days since the game came out, many have noted how amusing it is that Grand Theft Auto VI has made caring about your girlfriend one of its first challenges. The game’s “Lucia will appreciate this” notification is its first viral meme, and the source of both incel crashouts (“woke slop … so obvious it was made by women”) and earnest appreciation. (One of the first clips to spread online was of streamer Stable Ronaldo painting Jason and Lucia's bedroom one color before recoiling in horror: What if she hates that shade?).

Sources indicate that lucia is a destabilizing event not just for gamers, but for Grand Theft Auto—a damning yet fascinating example of gaming culture’s priorities on its biggest stage. GTA has always been a series of warring ambitions: violent Rube Goldberg machine, Karl Ove Knausgaard–esque obsession with quotidian details, and thrilling Hollywood blockbuster all in one. These disparate aims are often in conflict with one another, and one way to read the series’ heretofore exclusively male focus is as an attempt to thread this needle. By tossing all of its commentary under the carpet of “satire," Rockstar can also use a veneer of meanness to argue that the games’ misogyny is actually an intentional lambasting, much like everything else in GTA.

Recent findings suggest that but taking a woman seriously, and making her colead with a male character, requires an entire rethinking of what Grand Theft Auto is. “It’s a product of the story we’re trying to tell,” Grand Theft Auto VI codirector Rob Nelson said when asked by The Guardian if this is the first Grand Theft Auto to encourage empathy from players. “We’ve tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.”.

This is an extremely roundabout way of saying that, in this Grand Theft Auto, Rockstar asks gamers to grow up—and punishes them with narrative consequences if they don’t take the game up on the offer.

In a recent development, the funny thing about Grand Theft Auto VI’s gamified empathy is that, like everything else in a video game, it has to teach the player how to accomplish that goal. The game does this through prompting players to do chores, but also through Jason’s characterization. Throughout the game, Rockstar has to convey what its writers believe a well-adjusted man looks like—or at least what constitutes a man well-adjusted enough to earn the respect of a woman like Lucia, who walks out on him when he tries to exclude her from some of his more dangerous criminal activities.

Industry observers note that to that end, there are an abundance of moments in the game where Jason demonstrates the virtues of being respectful and maintaining boundaries, several of which are a departure from GTA series norms. There are no sex workers in the game anymore (though there are strip clubs). While Jason and Lucia can break up depending on the player’s choices, there are no other options for committed or casual romance.

The money you steal is ostensibly for Jason and Lucia to use together: so they can get away and start over with their young son, who’s currently entrusted to a relative. Casual conversations between strangers players meet on the road make Jason’s respectful nature both a point and a punchline. There’s one man who’s looking for his missing wife after a night of partying. When he starts to brag about her sexual dexterity, Jason interjects to say, “Hey. Let’s draw a line, bud.”.

In a recent development, in some ways, this is all rather embarrassing—though in a different way than the weapons-grade sexism of Grand Theft Autos past. One ought to feel a twinge of shame while marveling at any entertainment franchise for including a woman. Yet Grand Theft Auto VI is being graded on a curve. It has a near-perfect Metacritic score in large part for its depiction of Lucia, and for Jason’s relationship to her. The context speaks to a state of arrested development, both in Grand Theft Auto and in big-budget games writ large.

It has been revealed that none of this changes the fact that Lucia really is one of the most well-realized video game characters in a digital city unlike any other. But perhaps her inclusion is less an apology for GTA’s past, and more of a concession to how out of step the series had become with the culture. Because if you’re meant to have empathy for one character, the natural next question is, “Well, what about everyone else?".

Rockstar’s maniacal pursuit of verisimilitude goes a long way here. The game’s animations are so realistic that in GTA VI, shooting unarmed civilians is legitimately unsettling. It’s also disincentivized by a “criminal profile” rating that will mark your character “irredeemable” if you engage in too much wanton violence. (This is not a “game over”—it merely locks players out of achieving a happy ending unless they restart from before their murder spree.) These sorts of limits have become another reliable source of outrage directed at the game, with rage baiters drumming up controversy over Rockstar’s decision to, for example, not permit players to shoot up a nightclub.

This is the tricky reality of encouraging empathy for “those who want to,” as Nelson put it. Rockstar has certain intentions, but so do players—and managing both is the great challenge of making any video game. Empathy is a shock to GTA’s system and to the audience alike.

Replicating humanity with computer software is a daunting and costly task, and one that only Rockstar seems to have the limitless resources to pursue. Those resources—the luxury to work as long as necessary to complete Grand Theft Auto VI, and the obscene amount of money it cost (our only solid figure is “less than $1.5 billion”)—are rapidly dwindling in the video game business, as all available tech funding is vacuumed up by AI companies and private equity loots what’s left. Grand Theft Auto VI may very well be one of one: the most expensive game ever and the last of its kind, the peak of Rockstar’s ambition and also of every significant-budget video game. Here, at the end of everything, the biggest of video games has finally decided that it’s time to try empathy. And for a woman, even, should gamers choose (and not all will).

It’s a bit of an indictment of the billion-dollar video game industry that the most expensive game in history is also the first major game to commit to a realistic heterosexual relationship. Grand Theft Auto VI deserves many of the accolades it instantly garnered upon release, but the nature of its accomplishment is not yet fully understood. It’s possible that what Rockstar has built is less a monument to video games’ potential than a magnificent funeral pyre, a testament to how things might’ve turned out if Rockstar’s priorities—and those of everyone chasing after its vision of what video games could be—were just a little bit different.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you or someone on your shopping list wants a latest smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own manufacturer, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

The Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Sources indicate that where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

In a recent development, you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

For an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

Sources indicate that as a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET notes Android consumers can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

In a recent development, based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

Industry observers note that while the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android customers, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

The Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

Sources indicate that CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

Industry observers note that in CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

Still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another company drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

Sources indicate that I think it must be pretty hard to buy gifts for folks who love RPGs if you yourself are not familiar with them, because as I’ve discovered today while perusing the internet for ideas, most searches for RPG-themed gifts get you into the territory of tabletop RPGs rather than video game RPGs. Don’t get me wrong, I love a good TTRPG, but sometimes that’s not what you’re looking for exactly.

This is a guide to shopping for the RPG-lover in your life, someone who you know really likes a good role-playing video game with stats that go up as you level up, a nice significant fantasy world of some sort, stuff you can equip to make yourself stronger, probably a party of heroes adventuring together, and possibly some interesting moments where you can make choices that influence what happens next. There are a lot of games that fall into this category, and the RPG-lover in your life may or may not like some or all of these. So as with all gifts, try to get to know the person you’re gifting something to just a little and make sure you’re getting, say, a game for a system they actually own, or a piece of merchandise for one they already played and liked.

Industry observers note that with that in mind, here you are! 12 ideas!

Don’t worry, this list won’t be all straight-up games, but I did want to sprinkle a few recent releases in here to hopefully give you some options of newer games to gift that might broaden your giftee’s horizons. Trails in the Sky 1st ChapterÂ is a remake, released last year, of the original Trails in the Sky, which is the start of an excellent RPG that’s nonetheless (I think) overlooked by a lot of general RPG fans. The remake itself looks really nice, and the music is incredible. If you know someone who already has 1st Chapter in their library, 2nd Chapter came out this year too!

I’m not a huge collector of video game-themed merchandise, especially stuff that’s really obviously “gamer”, you know? But I have to admit these towels get me every time. It’s a genuinely funny play on a death screen from an iconic RPG series that anyone who’s touched a Souls game will probably find at least somewhat amusing.

The Adventures of Elliot is another release from this year, and while it’s not my personal favorite RPG, it’s got a lot going for it and a ton of RPG fans seemed to really dig it. Not a traditional turn-based RPG, this game instead has a singular main character, Elliot, who can switch between several different weapon types in action combat to dispatch monsters. It’s got that gorgeous HD-2D look that Square Enix has been using to marry a retro feel with modern visuals, and a pretty interesting story involving time travel to see the same world across multiple eras.

I’ve been seeing these little music boxes around for a bunch of different games, and I think they’re a really neat idea. But for an RPG fan, the absolute safest and best bet for a theme they’ll recognize is one from Final Fantasy. FF7 has several different ones, including both Tifa and Aerith’s themes, and there are more on the Square Enix store if you want to check that out or look for a music box for a specific game.

I tried to recommend several different kinds of RPGs on this list, depending on what the RPG gamer in your life most often plays. Beast of Reincarnation is a new game from the Pokemon developers, out this year, but it’s a far cry from what Pokemon is. Instead of capturing monsters, you and a single creature partner fight off blight-diseased enemies and explore a post-apocalyptic world using nature-based powers. It’s a game about humans, nature, and human nature, and might appeal especially to fans of the NieR games on aesthetic alone.

It has been revealed that hell yeah I’m recommending a dang notebook and pen. Who doesn’t love these? Seriously. As an RPG lover I frequently end up taking notes while playing games, either to solve puzzles, remember who the heck characters with fancy names are, or just doodling. And there are so many very cool notebooks and pens out there! You can go two directions with this. You can get something that has a very fantastical outward appearance, like this journal, or you could get a really nice-quality, plain notebook (the paper quality on this one is excellent and feels good to write on). For pens, you could get some colorful gel pens (everyone loves colors) or get a little fancy with it and introduce them to the world of fountain pens. This fountain pen is inexpensive and totally fineâif they really get into them, they may want to upgrade on a future holiday, but keep it simple for now.

This is coming out on December 3, so in just a few days: it’s Xenoblade 3 on Switch 2! Xenoblade 3 is already an excellent game, its Switch 2 version will include a upcoming recruitable character and a quest to obtain them, a new battle mode, newly-voiced event scenes, and it’s in 4K with a glorious 60fps. Check in first to see if the person already has this game on Switch, though, as the upgrade pack by itself to the Switch 2 edition is admittedly a bit cheaper.

It has been revealed that I love video game cookbooks. The ones by author Chelsea Monroe-Cassel are responsible for teaching me to cook in the first place! My two favorites of hers are the World of Warcraft Official Cookbook (and its sequel, Latest Flavors of Azeroth) and The Elder Scrolls Cookbook. All three are fun, easy to follow for novice cooks, and the recipes you end up with are both tasty and unique, often introducing me to ingredients I had never used before. The photography is also lovely, so even if your giftee doesn’t cook, they make a nice collector’s item for fans of the games. If neither of these games appeal, there’s a whole host of other video game cookbooks out there to choose from.

I dunno, I just wish someone would buy this for me. It’s cute and, if you like Undertale, actually extremely funny. Trust me, you’ll know if the RPG fan in your life likes Undertale.

Industry observers note that I’m genuinely not sure what it is, but every time I go to Japan for work, someone asks me to get them one of these Dragon Quest slimes. They come in several different versions at varying prices, so take your pick if you know someone who loves Dragon Quest.

Oh my God. These…are hilarious. For those who loved last year’s hit RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, these slippers are sure to get a laugh when unwrapped. They’re a hilarious tribute to a character who was obsessed with collecting monster feet, and they look extremely comfy to boot. Possibly a good gift even if someone didn’t play Expedition 33 on sheer utility.

In a recent development, yeah, really. I’m personally ambivalent about getting gift cards, as if that’s all you’re getting someone it can seem a tad thoughtless. But if you’re shopping for a kid who’s getting multiple things, or a secret Santa you don’t know well, this can be an okay choice. A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever RPG has been on their wishlist (though you can also just peek at their wishlist and buy one for them). You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles for those that own them. Take your pick.

In a recent development, the Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out, had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6. The data highlights that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video. That was a 9% slide from the Week 11 Thursday Night Football matchup in 2025 featuring the Upcoming England Patriots and New York Jets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Looking at week-over-week, the November 12 matchup this year between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants drew 16.27 million viewers, and was up 17% compared to the Week 10 matchup in 2025 featuring the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos. Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per game. One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by a score of 26-3. The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to. Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations. GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every few months, Grinding Gear Games resurfaces with livestreams to showcase all the newly introduced toys in the latest updates for Path of Exile 1 and 2. They play out quite differently from your usual game announcements, cutting straight to showing new gameplay features ahead of any preamble.

In a recent development, according to Path of Exile co-game director Jonathan Rogers, this is a key part of Path of Exile's success over the last 13 years. Speaking at games industry conference DevGAMM FTW!, he explained how GGG came up with a winning formula for PoE's seasonal update schedule.

Sources indicate that the announcement streams aren't just marketing, he explained, they help dictate what kinds of things the team should focus on with every enhancement. If it doesn't sound exciting enough to rally players around a new league, it doesn't get made.

After a teaser trailer reveals the theme and title of the league a few weeks before the full announcement, the stream dives right into the juiciest details—an approach that Rogers believes is paramount when it comes to selling the update.

Rogers says he's seen some "truly terrible livestreams for game announcements," before slipping in a quick jab: "Blizzard I'm looking at you.".

According to recent reports, I've watched enough Diablo 4 upcoming season streams to know exactly what he's talking about even if I don't quite agree that it's strictly a bad way to do it. Blizzard typically likes to lead with some introductions before having individual developers break down what's coming in an revision.

In a recent development, admittedly, these can drag on for too long, especially if you don't particularly care about percentage changes to some item or stat. But I appreciate hearing the thought process behind each decision from the people responsible for that aspect of the game. In a time when certain very vocal segments of the audience prefer to think of studios as machines, it's a good way to remind people that real human beings are behind it all.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

That said, I think Rogers' specific point about too many studios wasting everyone's time by holding the best announcements for last is often true. For something like a latest update to an ongoing game, everyone is watching to find out why this one is worth logging back in for. I want to see the standout details so I don't feel like I wasted 45 minutes for something I'm not that into.

Sometimes I do like the build-up and eventual payoff for a substantial reveal, though, like the way Blizzard dropped Diablo 5 at the end of the Diablo portion of this year's BlizzCon or how Larian surprised everyone with Divinity last year. Certain games earn the theatrics. If anything, Rogers' approach just underlines how important it is for studios to read the room and craft their announcements around the things that will actually spark interest rather than putting everyone to sleep.

According to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c Thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with consumers searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night Football also saw a big dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's latest open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. Given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together. However, there was one huge event that didn't include David Schwimmer's character, and there's a specific reason why. While Ross's absence from this particular scene was unfortunate, it did lead to a clever joke and a nod to something the character had become notorious for.

The end of Season 6 of Friends was a significant one. Chandler had done too good a job throwing Monica off the scent of his planned proposal – so much so that it seemed like she was actually considering Richard's proposal of marriage and a family – and was frantic to correct the situation. The big twist came when he came rushing back to the apartment, being made to believe he was too late, only to find Monica waiting for him with a proposal of her own.

No, David Schwimmer and Friends weren't "on a break," he was just busy overseas when the engagement scene was filmed.

Sources indicate that as Friends co-creator David Crane pointed out on the DVD commentary, all of David Schwimmer's scenes for the two-part Season 6 finale had to be filmed in the first week because the actor was in England filming Band of Brothers for HBO. Crane spoke about having to film the scene without Schwimmer, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that it was frustrating not having him because you feel as though there's a major event on the show, Monica and Chandler are engaged, and all the friends run in, but not quite all the friends. The moment still works, and it's still moving, but it would have been nice to have him for that, but we were not prepared to film that scene the previous week.

While all of the drama between Monica and Chandler was going on throughout "The One with the Proposal," Ross was busy breaking up with college student Elizabeth (a cliffhanger involving her revealing she's pregnant was discussed for the season finale, but ultimately scrapped). From what it sounds like, that was all filmed during the first week of production for these final episodes. The grand finale involving Chandler and Monica wasn't filmed until later.

As you'll recall, as the gang is celebrating with a group hug, Phoebe points out that "Ross isn't here!" to which Rachel responds, "Oh, hell, he's done this three times. He knows what it's about!" It's a funny way to acknowledge and then dismiss Ross's absence from his sister and best friend's engagement, while also firing a shot at Ross's "three-divorce guy" reputation. As Crane put it, that was the silver lining to the situation, after debating whether or not to point out the lack of Ross in the scene:.

Industry observers note that there was a lot of debate. Do you need to acknowledge the fact that Ross isn't here? Or do you just let it go? And it actually gave us a really good joke.
